MASH UP: Best OF [6269]

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
There were several fantastic moments from this year in terms of confrontations and some of our best investigations.

Unique Selling Point:
We are going to take 6 of our best stories from this year and look back at the moments that made them memorable and we are going to write to them with LINKS from Derek at Mnet's building. He will be pulling out those moments and helping our audience remember them. We want him to do it in a creative way - walking about the Mnet building, and the new multichoice building.

Summary:
My idea is to imagine If Carte Blanche were a person: who would they be? At 35, they’re a millennial: wiser and already preparing for 2023. BUT IN ORDER TO LOOK FORWARD (TAKE A DEEP BREATH) CARTE BLANCHE FIRST LOOKS BACK TO SEE WHAT ADVENTURES WE HAD IN 2022… (QUICK 4 SECOND VISUAL MASHUP EDITED TOGETHER…)
Who can forget the moments of the KZN shipping containers being tossed around like children's toys in the KZN floods. "we witnessed Kwa-Zulu Natal disappearing under April’s floodwater… we saw shipping containers tossed about like children’s toys and houses crumble to pieces.
And the moment where Mac watched a family grieve as they retrieved their loved one: Mac LINK “...just hearing the child cry as they retrieved the body, the family walking off, I never be able to describe to anyone what that was like…”
PRESENTER: CARTE BLANCHE PURSUED THE STORIES INSIDE THE STORIES -
VO: …Analyzing if the South African National Defense Force would have a smaller, nimbler future as it battles for survival in a world where defence technology costs money, and our budgets keep shrinking…

Bus wars story: the moment where we watch the bus driver be shot at and survive! And derek can mention masa's link about the poor bus drivers:
MASA LINK: I'm shocked how terrified these drivers were to talk to us... afraid that their attackers may come back and finish them off. They are bus drivers, not soldiers at war.
Then we can talk about the police dockets story where derek has to take off running after the criminal... we would say something like: as far as confrontations go, they don't always go as planned....
PRESENTER: WE CONFRONTED ALLEGED CRIMINALS… (Wide LS)
Then we will have the moments of MASA confronting the electricity meter criminals: Going undercover we revealed two men allegedly illegally slowing down or stopping electricity meters so the rate payer pays less or even nothing for their electricity usage. Of course we asked them why…
Case study 1: YASH: I swear an oath. I’m a Christian – I never done slowing down meters.
Case study 2 SPARKY: People only do this out of The pressure, like this is become too much for us. We cannot afford to pay the rate. I don't. I don't do this.

Then we will have nicky's vaccine certificate story - where mac is shouting at guy with hat as another memorable moment.
PRESENTER: WE EVEN CONFRONTED THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR CATCHING CRIMINALS (said a bit of tongue and cheek and a smirk
Mac: We have you accepting a bribe, tata…
Magadla: “I went to borrow money from another guy, because I was in a bind, you see.”
PRESENTER: WE DO SEE… AND WE LIKE TO SEE FIRST HAND WHICH RESULTS IN SOME OF OUR IMPACTFUL INVESTIGATIONS.
VO: …like when we travelled a thousand kilometers following hundreds of trucks carrying manganese.
“Ronelle: The magnitude of pollution is huge. The values are five times the allowed national standard.”
PRESENTER: HIDDEN IN PLAIN SIGHT, NO ONE KNEW HOW DANGEROUS THIS MINED MINERAL - A KEY COMPONENT IN STEEL AND LITHIUM BATTERIES - COULD BE, UNTIL WE UNEARTHED ITS DIRTY SECRETS… (Loud trucks dumping in small town)
VO: A dangerous neurotoxin, Manganese dust or fumes can cause permanent brain damage resulting in parkinsonian symptoms…
VO: Also concealed behind incomprehensible road death statistics we showed how unsafe free state roads are: which as a central province all highways pass through - like this one - which cost R736 million over 3 years.
Truck driver “This is how people have to drive on these roads, every which way, in the middle, next to the road- you can’t even drive next to the road anymore. How ridiculous is this?!
George: So you have a department just taking salaries – you are not funding them to do their work and you are contracting this out to contractors who don’t have a clue how to build the roads. And that is the crux of the problem.
VO: Here we showed that potholes aren’t just hazardous for vehicles but lethal.
Mac: When you arrive at a scene what is the first thing that goes through your mind?
Johann: Anger, Anger. Just imagine yourself getting there and you see bodies lying there and it's due to potholes.
PRESENTER/VO: FROM DEADLY TOXINS TO KILLER POTHOLES, CARTE BLANCHE IS THE KIND OF PERSON WHO SEEKS THE TRUTH, BECAUSE ONLY THAT CAN BRING CHANGE…

Script:


VO: After 35 years of Carte Blanche, you’d think we’d seen it all…
Soundup: Mashup of clips
But 2022 still surprised us…
Surprising …
Soundup: This is not fit for human consumption.
YOU’VE ALWAYS HAD THE RIGHT TO SEE IT ALL…HI THERE HANDSOME… DEF BETTER LOOKING THAN THAT GUY (POINTING AT MAC). (LOOKING AT DEVI) AND ALWAYS NICE TO SEE YOU! SORRY, I DIGRESS. MAKING SURE NOTHING IS HIDDEN FROM VIEW MEANS CONFRONTING THOSE WITH SERIOUS QUESTIONS TO ANSWER… NOT SOMETHING THAT ALWAYS GOES TO PLAN.
VO: Like when we confronted this man during an investigation into the alleged theft of police dockets. One look at our cameras and he was suddenly overcome with the need for exercise.
Derek: If you’re not guilty… why are you’re running away….
VO: And when we do get answers, the excuses are often Oscar worthy. Take this alleged electricity metre hacker, for example. Confronted by Masa, he looked for divine intervention.
Masa: This conversation we’re having where you’re lying is not going to work.
Case study 1: YASH: I swear an oath. I’m a Christian – I never done slowing down meters.
Masa: you are a christian who is slowing down electricity meters.
VO: Not even those entrusted with upholding the law are spared our confrontations: but, credit where credit’s due, they certainly think on their feet - even when caught red-handed.
Mac: We have you accepting a bribe, tata…
Magadla: “I went to borrow money from another guy, because I was in a bind, you see.”
VO: And even when faced with endless obstacles, we make sure our questions are heard!
Mac: confronting guy in covid certificate story - shouting at him through fence
PRESENTER LINK: BUT IT'S NOT ALL HIDE AND SEEK. IN MORE THAN 3 DECADES ON AIR, WE’VE COVERED STORIES BRIMFUL OF HUMAN DRAMA AND RAW EMOTION. THIS YEAR WAS NO DIFFERENT.
VO: In April, Mac witnessed the tragic aftermath of the floods in KwaZulu Natal.
Mac LINK “...just hearing the child cry as they retrieved the body, the family walking off, I never be able to describe to anyone what that was like…”
VO: And, as always, these stories impact us - the tellers - too. A story this year on the violence unleashed on long-distance bus operators left Masa wondering how the drivers go to work each day knowing their lives are in danger.
MASA LINK: I'm shocked how terrified these drivers were to talk to us... afraid that their attackers may come back and finish them off. They are bus drivers, not soldiers at war.
PRESENTER: DOCKET THEFT, FAKE VACCINE CERTS, AND BUS ATTACKS. THESE ARE CHILLING STORIES OFTEN INVOLVING DANGEROUS PEOPLE. SOMETIMES, THOUGH, WE TELL STORIES ABOUT THE DANGER LURKING IN LESS OBVIOUS PLACES. THE MINING AND TRANSPORT OF MANGANESE - A MINERAL IN PLENTIFUL SUPPLY IN SOUTH AFRICA AND GREAT DEMAND OVERSEAS.
VO: We followed hundreds of trucks carrying this much in demand commodity across the country, highlighting concerns around its impact on people’s health.
Dirk: My short-term memory about everything is not that good. I get angry very quickly, and I wasn’t like that before, never before.
Turns out it’s a neurotoxin transported freely everyday. In fact we found ourselves hitting the road quite often in 2022, something even to do stories on the roads themselves.
VO: Like this one, which cost hundreds of millions, but you can’t even drive on…
Truck driver “You can’t even drive next to the road anymore. How ridiculous is this?!
VO: Along the way, we were left in no doubt about the deadly impact of potholes.
(Visuals of bus)
VO: Yes, it’s been quite a year for Carte Blanche: And, because we believe Truth Brings Change, we look forward to 2023 where we’ll do it all again.
